# SAFBox STIG deviations

<!-- Generated by scripts/deviations-doc.sh from
     ansible/roles/hardening/vars/{deviations,not_applied}.yml,
     verify/safbox-rhel10-stig-overlay/{known-defects,baseline-titles}.yml
     and verify/thresholds/{release,build}.yml.
     Do not edit; change those files and regenerate. -->

SAFBox applies the DISA RHEL 10 STIG with the Ansible Lockdown
RHEL10-STIG role and validates it with the MITRE RHEL 10 STIG baseline
through the SAFBox overlay (`verify/safbox-rhel10-stig-overlay`). The
pins are in `ansible/group_vars/all/main.yml` and the overlay's
`inspec.yml`. The aim is a usable, documented security state, not a
clean report: every requirement SAFBox does not meet is either a
deviation listed here or a failing finding in the scan.

## Deviations

Requirements SAFBox deliberately does not apply. The hardening role
switches each one off with the Lockdown role's per-rule variable, and the
overlay marks it Not Applicable (impact 0.0) with the justification
below. Reason codes: `usability` (relaxed for the non-expert audience),
`content-defect` (an upstream role or profile bug, retired when the fix
is pinned) and `deploy-time` (only the deploying environment can satisfy
it).

| STIG ID | Rule | Requirement | Reason | Lockdown variable | Justification |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| RHEL-10-000510 | SV-280935 | Encrypt all local disk partitions that require at-rest protection | deploy-time | `rhel10stig_000510` | SAFBox is distributed as a virtual machine template and cannot encrypt its own disks. Any key that let the template boot unattended would be shared by every copy, so SAFBox does not presently provide encryption within the VM itself. Data at rest encryption should be implemented by the hypervisor or storage layer of the deploying environment. |
| RHEL-10-600425 | SV-281197 | Maintain an account lock until an administrator releases it | usability | `rhel10stig_600425` | SAFBox is an appliance for operators who may be its only administrator. A lock that only an administrator can release can leave nobody able to log in. Where pam_faillock locks an account, the lock instead expires after the pam_faillock default of 10 minutes. |
| RHEL-10-600415 | SV-281195 | Lock the root account until an administrator releases it after three failed logons | usability | `rhel10stig_600415` | Root is the recovery account of last resort on the console of a SAFBox that may have a single operator. Locking it until an administrator releases it can leave the appliance unrecoverable without a rebuild. |
| RHEL-10-600100 | SV-281169 | 60-day maximum password lifetime for new users in /etc/login.defs | usability | `rhel10stig_600100` | SAFBox deploy accounts are created at first boot, log in with an SSH key and have no password. Tested: once such an account's password passed the 60-day maximum age, its key login was refused because a password change was required that a locked password cannot make. |
| RHEL-10-600160 | SV-281175 | Disable accounts after 35 days of inactivity | usability | `rhel10stig_600160` | SAFBox deploy accounts log in with an SSH key and have no password to keep active. Tested: 35 days after such an account's password expired, PAM disabled the account and refused its key login. |
| RHEL-10-500035 | SV-281103 | Panic the system on a critical audit processing failure | usability | `rhel10stig_500035` | A panic on an audit processing failure would halt SAFBox and take its services down. SAFBox rotates its audit logs instead (max_log_file_action = ROTATE) and reports audit failures to the kernel log. |
| RHEL-10-200601 | SV-280970 | Enable the fapolicy module (application allow-listing) | usability | `rhel10stig_200601` | SAFBox is an automation runner: its accounts run the InSpec profiles and Ansible playbooks they bring. fapolicyd judges the program that opens a file, and for InSpec, Ansible and Node.js packages an account installs, that program is an interpreter (CINC Auditor's Ruby, Python, Node.js), so it cannot allow a tool without allowing its interpreter to run any code; a rule on the process name is met by any link given that name. Tested with fapolicyd enforcing, as an account other than root: an InSpec profile with Ruby libraries, a playbook with its own module or filter plugin, a collection in the account's home, a Python virtual environment and an npm package were all refused, as were cp and git checkout of Ruby files. /home, /tmp, /var/tmp and /dev/shm are mounted noexec, so programs placed there cannot be run directly; that does not stop interpreters or rootless containers running code an account supplies, which is what a runner is for. fapolicyd stays installed (RHEL-10-200600) and is not enabled. |
| RHEL-10-200602 | SV-280971 | Employ a deny-all, permit-by-exception fapolicy policy | usability | `rhel10stig_200602` | The policy takes effect only while fapolicyd runs, and SAFBox does not enable fapolicyd (SV-280970, same reasoning). Its rules are left as the package installs them. |
| RHEL-10-200642 | SV-280985 | Forward audit records via TCP to a different system via rsyslog | deploy-time, until a site sets `safbox_remote_log_server` | `rhel10stig_200642` | The remote log server is the deploying site's. SAFBox forwards no logs until a site names its server (safbox_remote_log_server); the rule is then applied and this control evaluated. |
| RHEL-10-200644 | SV-280987 | Authenticate the remote logging server for off-loading audit logs via rsyslog | deploy-time | `rhel10stig_200644` | Remote log offload is provided by the deploying site's log server. SAFBox ships without one to authenticate. |
| RHEL-10-200645 | SV-280988 | Encrypt audit records off-loaded via rsyslog | deploy-time | `rhel10stig_200645` | Remote log offload is provided by the deploying site's log server. SAFBox ships without one to send encrypted records to. |
| RHEL-10-800060 | SV-281338 | At least two name servers configured | deploy-time | `rhel10stig_800060` | Name servers are provided by the deploying site's network, through DHCP or cloud-init. |
| RHEL-10-701230 | SV-281325 | Certificate status checking for multifactor authentication | deploy-time | `rhel10stig_701230` | PKI-based multifactor authentication is provided by the deploying site's PKI and identity service. SAFBox ships without one. |
| RHEL-10-701270 | SV-281329 | Validate PKI certificates by constructing a certification path to an accepted trust anchor | deploy-time | `rhel10stig_701270` | The trust anchors for PKI-based authentication are provided by the deploying site's PKI. SAFBox ships without one. |
| RHEL-10-701280 | SV-281330 | Map the authenticated PKI identity to a user or group account | deploy-time | `rhel10stig_701280` | The mapping of PKI identities to accounts is provided by the deploying site's identity service. SAFBox ships without one. |
| RHEL-10-600000 | SV-281166 | Require a boot loader superuser password | deploy-time | `rhel10stig_600000` | A boot loader password baked into the template would be shared by every copy. The deploying site sets it (grub2-setpassword). |
| RHEL-10-600010 | SV-281167 | Require a unique boot loader superuser name | deploy-time | `rhel10stig_600010` | The boot loader superuser and its password are set by the deploying site, so that no copy of the template shares them. |

## Rules not applied because their Lockdown task fails

Rules switched off only so that the hardening run completes, because the
Lockdown task errors on SAFBox. They are not deviations: the overlay does
not touch them, so the baseline control still runs and its result,
whatever it is, is locked in `verify/thresholds/` until the task is
fixed and the entry removed. The scan column says what that result is.

| STIG ID | Rule | Lockdown variable | Failure seen | Scan result |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| RHEL-10-300010 | SV-281008 | `rhel10stig_300010` | 'Set fact from output' reads discovered_crypto_policies_config.stdout, but the task that registers it runs only with rhel10stig_disruption_high, so it errors with "object of type 'dict' has no attribute 'stdout'" | passes: the FIPS crypto policy is set at installation, so the requirement is met without the task |
| RHEL-10-300040 | SV-281011 | `rhel10stig_300040` | The warning-count task's when item "(rhel10stig_sshd_config_ciphers not in discovered_openssh_server_ciphers.stdout" has an unclosed parenthesis: "Syntax error in expression: unexpected end of template, expected ')'" | passes: under the FIPS crypto policy set at installation, sshd offers only approved ciphers without the task |
| RHEL-10-701150 | SV-281317 | `rhel10stig_701150` | The task applies but has no effect: EL10 ships no /etc/systemd/coredump.conf, and lineinfile creates one holding ProcessSizeMax=0 outside any [Coredump] section, which systemd ignores; the baseline control then errors (NoMethodError: undefined method 'ProcessSizeMax' for nil), and an errored control fails the gate | skipped: with the task off there is no /etc/systemd/coredump.conf (EL10 ships it as a %ghost file, defaults in /usr/lib/systemd/coredump.conf), and the control's parse_config_file reports "Can't find file" and skips |
| RHEL-10-701160 | SV-281318 | `rhel10stig_701160` | As for RHEL-10-701150: Storage=none is written outside any [Coredump] section of a newly created /etc/systemd/coredump.conf, systemd ignores it, and the baseline control errors (undefined method 'Storage' for nil) | skipped: as for SV-281317, the control finds no /etc/systemd/coredump.conf and skips |

## Known baseline defects (not deviations)

Controls of the pinned MITRE baseline that report a wrong or
unevaluated result on SAFBox. They are not deviations: the control stays
in force and its result is locked as it is. Recorded in
`verify/safbox-rhel10-stig-overlay/known-defects.yml`.

| Rule | Scan result | Defect | Upstream issue |
|---|---|---|---|
| SV-281009 | fails | Checks FIPS mode with fips-mode-setup --check, which RHEL 10 removed. SAFBox is in FIPS mode from installation (fips_enabled is 1, asserted by the build and by safbox-fips-1). Never deviated. | [issue](https://github.com/mitre/redhat-enterprise-linux-10-stig-baseline/issues/6) |
| SV-281332 | fails | Passes the zone label "drop (default)" unquoted to firewall-cmd --zone, which bash rejects, so the zone's ports, protocols and services are never evaluated. | not yet filed |
| SV-281333 | fails | As for SV-281332. | not yet filed |
| SV-281001 | fails | Treats the virtual machine as a container ("OpenSSH Server is installed but not approved for the container environment"). | not yet filed |
| SV-281296 | fails | As for SV-281001. | not yet filed |
| SV-281036 | passes | Calls input('var_log_messages_group') inside the matcher block, where it resolves no value even though the input is declared with a default (or set in an inputs file), and the comparison then passes whatever the group owner is. Setting the input does not help. | not yet filed |
| SV-281224 | fails | Reads Banner through the sshd_config resource, which does not follow the Include of /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/, so the Banner the hardening sets there is reported as not set. | not yet filed |

### The build context

The build-time gate scans the build VM before it is ever rebooted after
hardening, so settings that take effect at boot are not yet in force and
`verify/thresholds/build.yml` locks more failures: high 5, medium 102, low 0. Failing
only there:

| SV-281162 | medium | RHEL 10 must generate audit records for all account creations, modifications, disabling, and termination events that affect "/var/log/lastlog". |
| SV-281163 | medium | RHEL 10 must generate audit records for all uses of the "chmod", "fchmod", "fchmodat", and "fchmodat2" syscalls. |
| SV-281164 | medium | RHEL 10 must generate audit records for all uses of the "chown", "fchown", "fchownat", and "lchown" syscalls. |
| SV-281233 | medium | RHEL 10 must prevent files with the "setuid" and "setgid" bit set from being executed on the "/boot" directory. |
| SV-281248 | medium | RHEL 10 must prevent special devices on nonroot local partitions. |
| SV-281322 | medium | RHEL 10 must disable the kdump service. |

## Settings a site will want to know about

- **Login banner.** SAFBox ships a short placeholder banner, not the DoD
  notice (`safbox_logon_banner` in `ansible/group_vars/all/main.yml`).
  Set your own in `ansible/local.yml`, and the same text for the
  overlay's `banner_message_text_cli`, `banner_message_text_ral` and
  `banner_message_text_gui` inputs in your site inputs file.
- **Remote logging is off by default.** SAFBox forwards no logs, and
  SV-280985 is a deploy-time deviation, until a site names its log
  server: set `safbox_remote_log_server` (and `safbox_remote_log_port`,
  `safbox_remote_log_protocol`, tcp or udp) in `ansible/local.yml`, and
  the overlay input `remote_log_server` to the same server in your site
  inputs file. The hardening then writes
  `/etc/rsyslog.d/99-forwarding.conf` for that server and SV-280985 is
  evaluated. SV-280987 and SV-280988 (TLS authentication and encryption
  of the forwarded records) remain deviations until the site also
  provides certificates and switches those rules on.
- **USB devices are blocked by default.** The hardening enables USBGuard
  with no rules and its implicit policy set to block, so no USB device is
  authorized. To allow one, list it with `usbguard list-devices` and
  allow it permanently with `usbguard allow-device -p <id>`, or write a
  rule set with `usbguard generate-policy` into
  `/etc/usbguard/rules.conf`.

## Changing the posture for your site

Each control is a knob. To apply a deviated requirement, remove its entry
from `deviations.yml` and its override from
`verify/safbox-rhel10-stig-overlay/controls/overlay.rb` together
(`scripts/deviations-check.sh` fails if they disagree), then regenerate
this guide. To switch a further rule off, or change a value the Lockdown
role applies, set its `rhel10stig_*` variable in `ansible/local.yml`. A
site that changes what is applied supplies its own threshold
(`docs/rebuild.md`, Site inputs and thresholds).
